title.zh: 卷二百九十七 列傳第五十六 孔道輔 鞠詠 劉隨 曹修古 郭勸 段少連
title.en: Volume 297 Biographies 56: Kong Daofu, Ju Yong, Liu Sui, Cao Xiugu, Guo Quan, Duan Shaolian
title.raw: 卷二百九十七 列傳第五十六 孔道輔 鞠詠 劉隨 曹修古 郭勸 段少連 Volume 297 Biographies 56: Kong Daofu, Ju Yong, Liu Sui, Cao Xiugu, Guo Quan, Duan Shaolian

sentences.zh: 孔道輔

translations.literal: Kong Daofu
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daofu

sentences.zh: 孔道輔，字原魯，初名延魯，孔子四十五代孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Daofu, styled Yuanlu, originally named Yanlu, was the forty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daofu, whose style was Yuanlu and whose original name was Yanlu, was a forty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 父勖，進士及第，為太平州推官，以殿中丞通判廣州。

translations.literal: His father Xun passed the jinshi examination, served as judicial reviewer in Taiping Prefecture, and was promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently administered Guangzhou as transit commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had passed the jinshi examination and served as a judicial reviewer in Taiping Prefecture before being promoted to Palace Attendant and appointed transit commissioner of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 會真宗東封，躬詣孔子祠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong made his eastern tour of enfeoffment, he personally visited the temple of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong undertook his eastern tour of enfeoffment, he went in person to the temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 帝問宰相：「孔氏今孰為名者？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "Who among the Kong clan is prominent today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his chief ministers, "Who among the Kong clan holds renown today?"

sentences.zh: 或言勖有治行，即召對，以為太常博士、知曲阜縣。

translations.literal: Someone said that Xun had a record of good governance; he was immediately summoned for audience and appointed Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and magistrate of Qufu County.
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied that Xun had a reputation for capable administration, and he was at once summoned for an audience and appointed Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and magistrate of Qufu County.

sentences.zh: 初，勖在廣州，以清潔聞，及被召，蕃酋爭持寶貨以獻，皆慰遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Xun was in Guangzhou, he was known for integrity; when he was summoned, tribal chiefs vied to present him with precious goods, but he comforted them and sent them all away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during his tenure in Guangzhou, Xun had been known for his integrity; when he was summoned to court, tribal chiefs competed to offer him precious goods, but he politely declined each of them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 後為御史臺推直官，累遷秘書監、分司南京，管勾祖廟，以尚書工部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: Later he served as investigating officer of the Censorate, was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Library and commissioner at the Southern Capital, supervised the ancestral temple, and retired as Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as an investigating officer in the Censorate, rose through successive appointments to Director of the Imperial Library and commissioner at the Southern Capital, supervised the ancestral temple, and retired with the rank of Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 後道輔卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: Later Daofu died at the age of eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu died later, at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 道輔幼端重，舉進士第，為寧州軍事推官，數與州將爭事。

translations.literal: Daofu was dignified and steady from youth; he passed the jinshi examination and served as military judicial reviewer in Ning Prefecture, often disputing matters with the prefectural commander.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Daofu was grave and steady in bearing. After passing the jinshi examination he served as military judicial reviewer in Ning Prefecture, where he frequently clashed with the prefectural commander over official matters.

sentences.zh: 有蛇出天慶觀真武殿中，一郡以為神，州將帥官屬往奠拜之，欲上其事。

translations.literal: A snake appeared in the Zhenwu Hall of the Tianqing Abbey; the whole prefecture regarded it as divine, and the prefectural commander led officials to offer sacrifices and bow to it, intending to report the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: When a snake appeared in the Zhenwu Hall of the Tianqing Abbey, the entire prefecture took it for a divine sign; the prefectural commander led his subordinates to offer sacrifices and bow before it, and planned to memorialize the event to the throne.

sentences.zh: 道輔徑前以笏擊蛇，碎其首，觀者初驚，後莫不歎服。

translations.literal: Daofu went straight forward and struck the snake with his tablet, smashing its head; the onlookers were at first startled, but afterward none failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu strode forward and struck the snake with his court tablet, crushing its head. The onlookers were startled at first, but afterward none failed to admire his resolve.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺丞、知仙源縣，主孔子祠事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Xianyuan County, in charge of affairs at the temple of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed magistrate of Xianyuan County, where he took charge of the temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 孔氏故多放縱者，道輔一繩以法。

translations.literal: The Kong clan had long had many who were unrestrained; Daofu bound them all with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Kong clan had long been prone to license, but Daofu held them all strictly to the law.

sentences.zh: 上言廟制庳陋，請加修崇，詔可。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the temple regulations were low and shabby and requested that they be renovated and elevated; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the temple precincts were mean and dilapidated and asked that they be renovated and enlarged; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后臨朝，召為左正言。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, he was summoned as Left Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian assumed regency, he was summoned to serve as Left Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 受命日，論奏樞密使曹利用，尚御藥羅崇勳竊弄威柄，宜早斥去，以清朝廷。

translations.literal: On the day he received his appointment, he argued and memorialized that Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong and Director of Imperial Medicines Luo Chongxun were secretly wielding power and should be expelled early to clarify the court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took office, he memorialized that Military Affairs Commissioner Cao Liyong and Director of Imperial Medicines Luo Chongxun were secretly manipulating power and ought to be removed at once so that the court might be set in order.

sentences.zh: 立對稱刻，太后可其言乃退。

translations.literal: He stood to answer and spoke sharply; the empress dowager approved his words and only then did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He stood before the throne and spoke with cutting force; the empress dowager approved his counsel, and only then did he withdraw.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為直史館、判三司理欠憑由司。

translations.literal: Before long he was made compiler of the Historiography Institute and concurrently judged the Three Departments Office for Recovery of Arrears and Vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute and given concurrent charge of the Three Departments Office for Recovery of Arrears and Vouchers.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，道除右司諫、龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: On an embassy to the Khitan, en route he was appointed Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and Gentleman in Waiting at the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: While on an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed en route Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and Gentleman in Waiting at the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 契丹宴使者，優人以文宣王為戲，道輔艴然徑出。

translations.literal: At a Khitan banquet for the envoys, actors made a play of the Cultured Propagator King; Daofu flushed with anger and went straight out.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for the envoys, Khitan actors staged a skit mocking the Cultured Propagator King; Daofu flushed with anger and walked out without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 契丹使主客者邀道輔還坐，且令謝之，道輔正色曰：「中國與北朝通好，以禮文相接。

translations.literal: The Khitan host for guests of honor invited Daofu to return to his seat and also ordered him to apologize; Daofu said with a stern countenance: "China and the Northern Court are on friendly terms and meet each other with ritual and decorum.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan master of ceremonies invited Daofu back to his seat and told him to apologize. Daofu said sternly, "China and the Northern Court are bound in amity and ought to meet each other with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 今俳優之徒，慢侮先聖而不之禁，北朝之過也。

translations.literal: Now these actors and mimes have insulted the former sage without being stopped—this is the fault of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your actors have openly mocked the former sage without restraint. That is a fault of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 道輔何謝！」

translations.literal: Why should Daofu apologize!"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I apologize?"

sentences.zh: 契丹君臣默然，又酌大卮謂曰：「方天寒，飲此，可以致和氣。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler and ministers were silent; then they poured a large goblet and said: "The weather is cold; drink this and harmony may be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler and his ministers fell silent. Then they filled a large goblet and said, "The weather is bitterly cold; drink this, and perhaps harmony may be restored.

sentences.zh: 道輔曰：「不和，固無害。」

translations.literal: Daofu said: "If there is no harmony, it is in fact no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Daofu replied, "If there is no harmony, that in itself does no harm."

sentences.zh: 既還，言者以為生事，且開爭端。

translations.literal: After he returned, critics said he had stirred up trouble and opened a quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, critics accused him of stirring up trouble and provoking a dispute.

sentences.zh: 仁宗問其故，對曰：「契丹比為黑水所破，勢甚蹙。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong asked the reason; he replied: "The Khitan were recently broken by the Heishui and their situation is very pressed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong asked why he had acted as he did, Daofu replied, "The Khitan were recently shattered by the Heishui tribes and are in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 平時漢使至契丹，輒為所侮，若不較，恐益慢中國。」

translations.literal: In ordinary times when Han envoys reach the Khitan they are always insulted; if we do not contend, I fear they will increasingly slight China."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Han envoys visit them they are routinely slighted; if we do not stand our ground, they will only grow bolder in their contempt for China."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 歷判吏部流內銓、糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He successively judged the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Internal Appointments and inspected capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as judge of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Internal Appointments and as inspector of capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 坐糾事不當，出知鄆州，徙青州。

translations.literal: Because his impeachment matters were improper, he was sent out to administer Yan Prefecture and then transferred to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because his impeachments were judged improper, he was sent out to administer Yan Prefecture and later transferred to Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還判流內銓，遷尚書兵部員外郎，復出知徐、許二州，徙應天府。

translations.literal: He returned to judge the Bureau of Internal Appointments, was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War, again went out to administer Xu and Xu Prefectures, and was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to judge the Bureau of Internal Appointments, was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War, was again sent out to administer Xu and Xu Prefectures, and was then transferred to Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，召為右諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was summoned as Right Remonstrating Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Mingdao era he was recalled as Right Remonstrating Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會郭皇后廢，道輔率諫官孫祖德、范仲淹、宋郊、劉渙，御史蔣堂、郭勸、楊偕、馬絳、段少連十人，詣垂拱殿伏奏：「皇后天下之母，不當輕議絀廢。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed, Daofu led ten remonstrating officials Sun Zude, Fan Zhongyan, Song Jiao, and Liu Huan, and censors Jiang Tang, Guo Quan, Yang Xie, Ma Jiang, and Duan Shaolian to the Hall of Hanging Bow, where they prostrated themselves and memorialized: "The empress is mother of the realm; one must not lightly discuss degrading and deposing her.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed, Daofu led ten remonstrators—Sun Zude, Fan Zhongyan, Song Jiao, and Liu Huan—and censors Jiang Tang, Guo Quan, Yang Xie, Ma Jiang, and Duan Shaolian to the Hall of Hanging Bow, where they prostrated themselves and declared, "The empress is mother of the realm; her deposition must not be debated lightly.

sentences.zh: 願賜對，盡所言。」

translations.literal: We beg to be granted audience to state all we have to say."
translations.idiomatic: We beg an audience so that we may speak our minds fully."

sentences.zh: 帝使內侍諭道輔等至中書，令宰相呂夷簡以皇后當廢狀告之。

translations.literal: The emperor had a palace attendant instruct Daofu and the others to go to the Secretariat and ordered Chief Minister Lü Yijian to inform them of the grounds on which the empress ought to be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace attendant to direct Daofu and his colleagues to the Secretariat and ordered Chief Minister Lü Yijian to explain the grounds for deposing the empress.

sentences.zh: 道輔語夷簡曰：「大臣之於帝后，猶子事父母也；

translations.literal: Daofu said to Yijian: "In relation to the emperor and empress, great ministers are like sons serving parents;
translations.idiomatic: Daofu said to Yijian, "A great minister stands toward the emperor and empress as a son toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 父母不和，可以諫止，奈何順父出母乎？」

translations.literal: when parents are not in harmony one may remonstrate to stop it—how can one comply with the father in expelling the mother?"
translations.idiomatic: When parents quarrel, a son may remonstrate to restore harmony. How can he comply with the father in driving out the mother?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡曰：「廢后有漢、唐故事。」

translations.literal: Yijian said: "Deposing an empress has Han and Tang precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian replied, "Deposing an empress has Han and Tang precedents."

sentences.zh: 道輔復曰：「人臣當道君以堯、舜，豈得引漢、唐失德為法邪？」

translations.literal: Daofu replied again: "A subject ought to guide his ruler with Yao and Shun—how can one cite Han and Tang lapses in virtue as models?"
translations.idiomatic: Daofu answered, "A subject ought to guide his ruler toward the example of Yao and Shun. How can one cite the moral failures of Han and Tang as precedent?"

sentences.zh: 夷簡不答，即奏言：「伏閣請對，非太平美事。」

translations.literal: Yijian did not answer and immediately memorialized: "Prostrating at the gate to request audience is not a fine affair of great peace."
translations.idiomatic: Yijian made no reply and at once memorialized, "Remonstrators blocking the gate to demand audience is no sign of a well-governed age."

sentences.zh: 於是出道輔知泰州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daofu was sent out to administer Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu was thereupon sent out to administer Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 明日晨，入至待漏，聞有詔，亟馳出城。

translations.literal: The next morning at dawn he entered and reached the waiting-for-the-water-clock station; hearing there was an edict, he hurriedly galloped out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning at dawn he arrived at the court waiting station; when he heard that an edict had been issued against him, he galloped out of the city at once.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徙徐州，又徙兗州，進龍圖閣直學士，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Xu Prefecture, then again to Yan Prefecture; he was advanced to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and promoted to Attendant-in-Chief of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Xu Prefecture and then to Yan Prefecture, advanced to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and promoted to Attendant-in-Chief of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 在兗三年，復入為御史中丞。

translations.literal: After three years in Yan he returned to the capital as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in Yan Prefecture he was recalled to serve again as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 道輔性鯁挺特達，遇事彈劾無所避，出入風采肅然，及再執憲，權貴益忌之。

translations.literal: Daofu was by nature upright, unyielding, and outstanding; in affairs he impeached without avoidance, and in coming and going his bearing was stern; when he again held the censorate, the powerful grew all the more to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu was by nature upright and unyielding, impeaching without fear in whatever matter arose; his bearing in public was always stern. When he again headed the censorate, the powerful resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 初，道輔與其父里中僦郭贄舊宅居之，有言於帝者曰：「道輔家近太廟，出入傳呼，非所以尊神明。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Daofu and his father in their home district rented Guo Zan's old residence to live in; someone said to the emperor: "Daofu's home is near the Imperial Ancestral Temple; his coming and going with attendants calling out is not the way to honor the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Daofu and his father had rented the old residence of Guo Zan in their home district. Someone told the emperor, "Daofu's house lies too close to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the calls of his attendants as he comes and goes fail to show proper reverence for the spirits."

sentences.zh: 即詔道輔他徙。

translations.literal: An edict immediately ordered Daofu to move elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once ordered Daofu to move elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 集賢校理張宗古上言，漢內史府在太廟堧垣中，國朝以來，廟垣下皆有官私第舍，謂不須避。

translations.literal: Collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents Zhang Zonggu memorialized that in Han the interior secretary's office was within the temple rampart, and since the founding of the dynasty there had been official and private residences below the temple wall, saying there was no need to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zonggu, collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, memorialized that in Han times the interior secretary's office had stood within the temple rampart, and that since the founding of the dynasty official and private residences had always lain below the temple wall, so that no avoidance was required.

sentences.zh: 帝出宗古通判萊州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zonggu out as transit commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zonggu out to serve as transit commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 道輔歎曰：「憸人之言入矣！」

translations.literal: Daofu sighed and said: "The words of the slanderer have entered!"
translations.idiomatic: Daofu sighed and said, "The slanderer's words have prevailed."

sentences.zh: 會受詔鞠馮士元獄，事連參知政事程琳。

translations.literal: He happened to receive an edict to investigate the case of Feng Shiyuan, which implicated Vice Grand Councillor Cheng Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to investigate the case of Feng Shiyuan, which implicated Vice Grand Councillor Cheng Lin.

sentences.zh: 宰相張士遜素惡琳，而疾道輔不附己，將逐之，察帝有不悅琳意，即謂道輔：「上顧程公厚，今為小人所誣，見上，為辨之。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Shisun had long hated Lin and also resented that Daofu would not attach himself to him; he intended to drive Daofu away, perceived that the emperor was displeased with Lin, and then said to Daofu: "His Majesty regards Lord Cheng with deep favor; now he is slandered by petty men—when you see the emperor, plead for him."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Shisun had long hated Lin and resented Daofu's refusal to align with him; intending to drive Daofu out, he perceived the emperor's displeasure with Lin and told Daofu, "His Majesty still holds Lord Cheng in high regard, yet petty men have slandered him. When you see the emperor, speak in his defense."

sentences.zh: 道輔入對，言琳罪薄不足深治。

translations.literal: Daofu entered for audience and said Lin's offense was slight and did not warrant severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu appeared before the throne and argued that Lin's offenses were slight and did not warrant severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝果怒，以道輔朋黨大臣，出知鄆州。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed angry and, on the grounds that Daofu was in faction with a great minister, sent him out to administer Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indeed angered and, charging Daofu with factionalizing on behalf of a great minister, sent him out to administer Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 已而道輔知為士遜所賣，頗憤惋。

translations.literal: Before long Daofu knew he had been sold out by Shisun and was quite resentful and aggrieved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Daofu realized that Shisun had betrayed him, and he was deeply aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 時大寒上道，行至韋城，發病卒，天下莫不以直道許之。

translations.literal: At the time the cold was severe as he took the road; when he reached Weicheng he fell ill and died; throughout the realm none failed to acknowledge him for the upright Way.
translations.idiomatic: He set out in bitter cold, fell ill at Weicheng, and died on the road. Throughout the realm men agreed that he had walked the path of integrity.

sentences.zh: 皇祐三年，王素因對語及道輔，仁宗思其忠，特贈尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangyou, Wang Su in an audience mentioned Daofu; Emperor Renzong recalled his loyalty and specially posthumously granted him Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangyou, Wang Su mentioned Daofu during an audience; Emperor Renzong recalled his loyalty and posthumously granted him the rank of Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子：宗翰。

translations.literal: Son: Zonghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zonghan.

sentences.zh: 子 宗翰

translations.literal: Son: Zonghan
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan

sentences.zh: 宗翰，字周翰。

translations.literal: Zonghan, styled Zhouhan.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan, whose style was Zhouhan,

sentences.zh: 登進士第，知仙源縣，而為治有條理，遇族人有恩，不以私故骫法。

translations.literal: passed the jinshi examination, administered Xianyuan County, and in governance was orderly; when he encountered clansmen in need he showed kindness but did not bend the law for private reasons.
translations.idiomatic: passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Xianyuan County. His administration was methodical; he showed kindness to kinsmen but never bent the law for private reasons.

sentences.zh: 王珪、司馬光皆上章論薦，由通判陵州為夔峽轉運判官，提點京東刑獄、知虔州。

translations.literal: Wang Gui and Sima Guang both memorialized recommending him; from transit commissioner of Ling Prefecture he became transport judge of the Kuizhou Gorge circuit, intendant of criminal justice in eastern capital circuit, and administrator of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui and Sima Guang both memorialized in his favor. He rose from transit commissioner of Ling Prefecture to transport judge of the Kuizhou Gorge circuit, then served as intendant of criminal justice in the eastern capital circuit and as administrator of Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城濱章、貢、兩江，歲為水齧。

translations.literal: The city bordered the Zhang and Gong rivers; every year it was gnawed by the water.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on the Zhang and Gong rivers, whose waters eroded its walls year after year.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐石為址，冶鐵錮之，由是屹然，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: Zonghan cut stone for foundations and smelted iron to bind them; thereby it stood firm, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan cut stone for new foundations and bound them with wrought iron, so that the walls stood firm; an edict commended his work.

sentences.zh: 歷陝、揚、洪、兗州，皆以治聞。

translations.literal: He successively administered Shan, Yang, Hong, and Yan Prefectures, and in all was known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession at Shan, Yang, Hong, and Yan Prefectures, winning renown for good governance at each.

sentences.zh: 哲宗初立求言，吏民上書以千數，詔司馬光采閱其可用者十五人，獨稱獎其二，乃宗翰與王鞏也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong first ascended and sought counsel, officials and commoners submitted memorials by the thousands; an edict ordered Sima Guang to select and review fifteen usable ones, singling out only two for praise—Zonghan and Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong first ascended the throne and called for counsel, officials and commoners submitted thousands of memorials. The throne ordered Sima Guang to select fifteen worthy submissions and singled out only two for special praise: Zonghan and Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，召為司農少卿，遷鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Agriculture and later transferred to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Agriculture and later promoted to Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 言：「孔子之後，自漢以來有褒成、奉聖、宗聖之號，皆賜實封或縑帛，以奉先祀。

translations.literal: He said: "Descendants of Confucius, since Han, have borne the titles Baocheng, Fengsheng, and Zongsheng, all granted substantive enfeoffments or silk to maintain ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Since Han times, descendants of Confucius have borne the titles Baocheng, Fengsheng, and Zongsheng, each granted substantive enfeoffment or silk stipends to maintain the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 至於國朝，益加崇禮。

translations.literal: As for our dynasty, honor has been further increased.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has honored them still more lavishly.

sentences.zh: 真宗東封臨幸，賜子孫世襲公爵，然兼領他官，不在故郡，於名為不正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong made his eastern tour and visited in person, he granted their descendants a hereditary ducal title, yet they also held other offices and were not in their native commandery—this was not correct in name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong made his eastern tour and visited in person, he granted their descendants a hereditary ducal title, yet they also held other offices and did not reside in their ancestral home—a title empty of its proper meaning.

sentences.zh: 講自今襲封之人，使終身在鄉里。」

translations.literal: I propose that from now on those who inherit the enfeoffment should spend their whole lives in their home district."
translations.idiomatic: I propose that hereafter the holder of the hereditary title should remain in his home district for life."

sentences.zh: 詔改衍聖公為奉聖公，不領他職，給廟學田萬畝，賜國子監書，立學官以誨其子弟。

translations.literal: An edict changed Yanshenggong to Fengshenggong, without holding other offices, granted ten thousand mu of temple-school land, bestowed books from the Directorate of Education, and established school officials to instruct their sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict changed the title from Yanshenggong to Fengshenggong, barred the holder from other offices, granted ten thousand mu of temple-school land, bestowed books from the Directorate of Education, and established school officials to instruct the clan's youth.

sentences.zh: 進刑部侍郎，屬疾求去，以寶文閣待制知徐州，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Minister of Justice, fell ill and requested leave, was appointed Gentleman in Waiting at the Hall of Treasured Literature and administrator of Xu Prefecture, and died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, fell ill and requested retirement, and was appointed Gentleman in Waiting at the Hall of Treasured Literature and administrator of Xu Prefecture, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 鞠詠，字詠之，開封人。

translations.literal: Ju Yong, styled Yongzhi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Yong, whose style was Yongzhi, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父勵，尚書膳部員外郎、廣南轉運使。

translations.literal: His father Li was Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Provisions and transport commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Provisions and as transport commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 詠十歲而孤，好學自立。

translations.literal: Yong was orphaned at ten, loved learning, and stood on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was orphaned at the age of ten but devoted himself to learning and made his own way in the world.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，試秘書省校書郎、知錢塘縣，改著作郎、知山陰縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was tried as collator of the Secretariat and magistrate of Qiantang County, and was changed to drafting officer and magistrate of Shanyin County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as collator of the Secretariat and magistrate of Qiantang County, and was later appointed drafting officer and magistrate of Shanyin County.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，以太常博士召為監察御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, Yong was summoned from his post as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple to serve as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演自亳州來朝，圖入相。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan came from Bozhou to court and plotted to enter the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan came from Bozhou to attend court, scheming to enter the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 詠言：「惟演憸險，嘗與丁謂為婚姻，緣此大用。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Weiyan is treacherous and dangerous; he once formed a marriage alliance with Ding Wei and through this was greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized, "Weiyan is treacherous and dangerous. He once allied himself with Ding Wei by marriage and rose to power through that connection.

sentences.zh: 後揣知謂奸狀已萌，懼牽連得禍，因此力攻謂。

translations.literal: Later, perceiving that Wei's treachery had already sprouted, fearing to be implicated and suffer disaster, he therefore vigorously attacked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later, sensing that Wei's treachery was about to be exposed, he feared being dragged down with him and turned fiercely against Wei.

sentences.zh: 今若遂以為相，必大失天下望。」

translations.literal: If he is now made chief minister, he will surely greatly lose the hope of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: If he is now made chief minister, the realm will surely lose all confidence in the court."

sentences.zh: 太后遣內侍持奏示之，惟演猶顧望不行。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent a palace attendant to show him the memorial, but Weiyan still hesitated and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent a palace attendant to show Weiyan the memorial, yet he still lingered and would not depart.

sentences.zh: 詠語諫官劉隨曰：「若相惟演，當取白麻廷毀之。」

translations.literal: Yong said to remonstrator Liu Sui: "If Weiyan is made chief minister, we should take the white hemp edict and tear it up in the court."
translations.idiomatic: Yong told the remonstrator Liu Sui, "If Weiyan is appointed chief minister, we should seize the white hemp edict of appointment and tear it apart in open court."

sentences.zh: 惟演聞，乃亟去。

translations.literal: When Weiyan heard, he hurriedly left.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyan heard this, he departed at once.

sentences.zh: 大安殿柱生芝草，召群臣就觀。

translations.literal: On a pillar of the Hall of Great Peace lingzhi grass grew; the emperor summoned the ministers to come view it.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi fungus sprouted on a pillar of the Hall of Great Peace, and the emperor summoned his ministers to come and view it.

sentences.zh: 詠言：「陛下新即位，河決未塞，霖雨害稼，宜思所以應災變。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; the river breach is not yet stopped and prolonged rain harms the crops—you ought to consider how to respond to these calamities and changes.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Your Majesty has only recently ascended the throne. The Yellow River breach remains unsealed and prolonged rains have ruined the harvest. You ought to consider how to respond to these portents of disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下以援進忠良、退斥邪佞為國寶，以訓勸兵農、豐積倉廩為天瑞。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to take promoting the loyal and good and removing the wicked and flatterers as the state's treasure, and taking instructing soldiers and farmers and filling the granaries as heaven's auspice.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take the promotion of loyal men and the removal of the wicked as the state's true treasure, and the training of soldiers and farmers and the filling of the granaries as heaven's true auspice.

sentences.zh: 草木之怪，何足尚哉！」

translations.literal: What is there to esteem in the marvel of plants and trees!"
translations.idiomatic: What is there to esteem in the freakish growth of plants?"

sentences.zh: 時王欽若復相，詠嫉欽若阿倚，數睥睨其短，欽若心忌之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Qinruo again became chief minister; Yong resented Qinruo's fawning and leaning, often glancing at his faults, and Qinruo inwardly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo had again become chief minister. Yong despised his sycophancy and repeatedly exposed his faults; Qinruo came to resent him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會詠兼左巡使，率府率崇俊入朝失儀，詠言崇俊少在邊，今老矣，此不足罪。

translations.literal: Yong happened also to be Left Patrol Commissioner; the commandery commander Chong Jun entered court with improper ceremony; Yong said Chong Jun had long been on the frontier and was now old—this was not enough to punish.
translations.idiomatic: Yong also served as Left Patrol Commissioner. When the commandery commander Chong Jun breached court protocol on entering audience, Yong argued that Chong Jun had spent his youth on the frontier and was now old—that this lapse was not worth punishing.

sentences.zh: 欽若奏詠廢朝廷儀，出通判信州。

translations.literal: Qinruo memorialized that Yong had discarded court ceremony and sent him out as transit commissioner of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo memorialized that Yong had disregarded court ceremony and had him sent out as transit commissioner of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又坐鞫陳絳獄失實，徙邵州。

translations.literal: He was again punished for investigating the Chen Jiang case with findings not matching facts and was transferred to Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was further punished when his investigation of the Chen Jiang case was found inaccurate and was transferred to Shao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 欽若卒，御史中丞王臻奏還詠殿中侍御史，為三司鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: When Qinruo died, Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhen memorialized to restore Yong as Palace Attendant Censor and make him Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: After Qinruo's death, Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhen memorialized for Yong's restoration as Palace Attendant Censor and appointment as Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 曹利用貶死，利用嘗所薦擢者多領兵守邊，朝廷欲罷去之，詠請一切毋治。

translations.literal: Cao Liyong was demoted and died; many whom Liyong had once recommended and promoted held military commands guarding the borders, and the court wished to remove them; Yong requested that all be left untried.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Liyong was demoted and died, many officers he had promoted still held border commands, and the court wished to remove them. Yong pleaded that they all be left in place without investigation.

sentences.zh: 天聖六年夏，大星晝隕，有聲如雷，詠條五事上之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Tiansheng a great star fell in daylight with a sound like thunder; Yong listed five matters and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year of Tiansheng a great star fell in broad daylight with a sound like thunder; Yong submitted a memorial listing five matters for the throne's attention.

sentences.zh: 因言：「太子少保致仕晁迥，雖老而有器識，宜蒙訪對，其必有補。」

translations.literal: He added: "Retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao Jiong, though old, has capacity and insight and ought to receive visits for audience—he will surely be of help.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The retired Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Chao Jiong, though advanced in years, still possesses wisdom and judgment and ought to be summoned for counsel; he would surely prove of benefit."

sentences.zh: 又言：「三司使胡則，丁謂黨也，性貪巧，不可任利權。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Three Departments Commissioner Hu Ze is of Ding Wei's faction; by nature greedy and artful—he must not be entrusted with profit authority."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Three Departments Commissioner Hu Ze belongs to Ding Wei's faction. Greedy and cunning by nature, he must not be entrusted with control over state revenues."

sentences.zh: 河北、京師旱饑，奏請出太倉米十萬石振饑民。

translations.literal: In Hebei and the capital circuits drought and famine struck; he memorialized to release one hundred thousand shi of grain from the Great Granary to relieve the hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and famine struck Hebei and the capital region, he memorialized to release one hundred thousand shi of grain from the Great Granary to feed the starving populace.

sentences.zh: 江、淮制置使鍾離瑾因奏計，多致東南物以賂權貴。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai Commissioner Zhongli Jin, while presenting his accounts, brought many goods from the southeast to bribe the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai Commissioner Zhongli Jin, while presenting his fiscal accounts, had brought vast quantities of goods from the southeast to bribe powerful officials.

sentences.zh: 詠請御史臺劾狀，帝面諭瑾亟還所部。

translations.literal: Yong requested the Censorate to impeach him; the emperor face-to-face instructed Jin to return quickly to his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yong requested that the Censorate impeach him; the emperor personally ordered Jin to return at once to his post.

sentences.zh: 以尚書禮部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事、權同判吏部流內銓，為三司鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites while also serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs and acting judge of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Internal Appointments, and became Vice Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites while concurrently serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, acting judge of the Bureau of Internal Appointments, and Vice Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 八年，特置天章閣待制，以詠及范諷為之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the post of Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall was specially established, with Yong and Fan Feng appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the court specially established the post of Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall and appointed Yong and Fan Feng to fill it.

sentences.zh: 判登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He judged the Petition Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to judge the Petition Review Office.

sentences.zh: 定國軍節度使張士遜入覲，冀得再用。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner of Dingguo Army Zhang Shisun came to audience hoping to be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shisun, military commissioner of the Dingguo Army, came to court hoping to be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 詠奏曰：「曹利用擅威福，士遜與之共事，相親厚，援薦以至相位。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized: "Cao Liyong monopolized authority and favor; Shisun served with him, were close and thick, and recommended and advanced each other to the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized, "Cao Liyong monopolized power and favor. Shisun served alongside him, they grew intimate, and through mutual patronage rose together to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 陛下以東宮僚屬用之，臣願割舊恩，伸公義，趣使之藩。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty employed him as an Eastern Palace subordinate; your subject wishes to sever old favor, extend public justice, and urge that he be sent to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty appointed him from among your Eastern Palace staff. I beg you to set aside old favor, uphold public justice, and send him back to his command at once."

sentences.zh: 士遜乃赴鎮。

translations.literal: Shisun thereupon went to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Shisun thereupon departed for his post.

sentences.zh: 明年詠卒。

translations.literal: The next year Yong died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yong died.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《道釋雜言》數十篇，別構淨室以居，自號「深寧子」。

translations.literal: He once wrote several tens of chapters of Miscellaneous Sayings on the Way and Buddhism, built a separate pure chamber to dwell in, and styled himself "Master Deep Tranquility."
translations.idiomatic: He had written several dozen essays entitled Miscellaneous Sayings on the Way and Buddhism, built a separate retreat in which to live, and styled himself Master Deep Tranquility.

sentences.zh: 劉隨，字仲豫，開封考城人。

translations.literal: Liu Sui, styled Zhongyu, was a native of Kaocheng in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sui, whose style was Zhongyu, was a native of Kaocheng in Kaifeng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以進士及第，為永康軍判官。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he served as judicial aide of Yongkang Army.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as judicial aide of Yongkang Army.

sentences.zh: 軍無城堞，每伐巨木為柵，壞，輒以他木易之，頗用民力。

translations.literal: The army post had no walls or battlements; every time they felled great trees for palisades and they broke, they replaced them with other timber, greatly using the people's labor.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison had no walls; whenever its timber palisades rotted, new logs had to be cut, imposing a heavy burden on the local populace.

sentences.zh: 隨因令環植楊柳數十萬株，使相連屬，以為限界，民遂得不擾。

translations.literal: Sui therefore ordered the planting in a ring of several hundred thousand willows so they linked together as a boundary, and the people were thus not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Sui therefore ordered several hundred thousand willows planted in a continuous ring to serve as a living palisade, sparing the people further hardship.

sentences.zh: 屬縣令受賕鬻獄，轉運使李士衡託令於隨，不從。

translations.literal: A subordinate magistrate took bribes and sold justice; Transport Commissioner Li Shiheng asked Sui to entrust the magistrate to him, but Sui refused.
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate magistrate took bribes and sold judgments, Transport Commissioner Li Shiheng asked Sui to hand the case over to him; Sui refused.

sentences.zh: 士衡憤怒，乃奏隨苛刻，不堪從政，罷歸，不得調。

translations.literal: Shiheng was angry and memorialized that Sui was harsh and exacting, unfit for government, dismissed him to return home, and he could not be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shiheng memorialized that Sui was harsh and unfit for office. Sui was dismissed and barred from further appointment.

sentences.zh: 初，西南夷市馬入官，苦吏誅索，隨為繩按之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when southwestern tribes sold horses to the government, they suffered from officials' extortion; Sui bound and investigated this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when southwestern tribes sold horses to the government, they had suffered extortion by officials; Sui investigated and punished the guilty.

sentences.zh: 既罷，夷人數百訴於轉運使曰：「吾父何在？」

translations.literal: After he was dismissed, several hundred tribesmen complained to the transport commissioner: "Where is our father?"
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal, several hundred tribesmen appealed to the transport commissioner, crying, "Where is our father?"

sentences.zh: 事聞，乃得調。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was able to be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 後改大理寺丞，為詳斷官。

translations.literal: Later he was changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and served as detailed adjudication officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed detailed adjudication officer.

sentences.zh: 李溥以贓敗，事連權貴，有司希旨不窮治，隨請再劾之，卒抵溥罪。

translations.literal: Li Pu was ruined by corruption; the case implicated the powerful, and the authorities curried favor and did not pursue it to the end; Sui requested a second impeachment and in the end brought Pu to conviction.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Pu was exposed for corruption in a case implicating powerful figures, the authorities curried favor and declined to pursue it fully. Sui demanded a second investigation and ultimately secured Pu's conviction.

sentences.zh: 晁迥薦通判益州，呂夷簡安撫川峽，又言其材，以太常博士改右正言。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong recommended him as transit commissioner of Yi Prefecture; Lü Yijian, pacification commissioner of the Sichuan Gorges, also spoke of his talent; from Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple he was changed to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong recommended him as transit commissioner of Yi Prefecture, and Lü Yijian, pacification commissioner of the Sichuan Gorges, also praised his ability. He was promoted from Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple to Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 數月，坐嘗為開封府發解巡捕官，而不察舉人，私以策辭相授，降監濟州稅，稍徒通判晉州。

translations.literal: Several months later, because he had once been Kaifeng's examination patrol officer and failed to scrutinize candidates, privately exchanging examination answers, he was demoted to supervise Jizhou taxes and later transferred as transit commissioner of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was punished for having served as Kaifeng's examination patrol officer without properly scrutinizing candidates who had exchanged examination answers in private. He was demoted to supervise Jizhou taxes and later transferred as transit commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還朝，遷右司諫，為三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was transferred to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and made Household Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was promoted to Right Remonstrator of the Secretariat and appointed Household Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 隨在諫職數言事，嘗言：「今之所切，在於納諫，其餘守常安靖而已。」

translations.literal: In his remonstrating office Sui often spoke on affairs; he once said: "What is urgent now lies in accepting remonstrance; the rest is merely keeping to convention and remaining tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In his remonstrating office Sui spoke out frequently. He once said, "What the times require above all is that remonstrance be heeded; everything else is mere routine and quietism."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「頻年水旱，咎在執事大臣忿爭不和。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In successive years flood and drought—the blame lies in the chief ministers' angry disputes and lack of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Years of flood and drought stem from the angry feuding of the chief ministers who will not work in harmony.

sentences.zh: 請察王欽若等所爭，為辨曲直。」

translations.literal: I request investigation of what Wang Qinruo and others dispute and judgment of right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to investigate the disputes of Wang Qinruo and his rivals and judge who is in the right."

sentences.zh: 又因星變言：「國家本支蕃衍，而定王之外，封策未行。

translations.literal: Because of a stellar anomaly he also said: "The state's root and branches flourish, yet beyond the Prince of Ding enfeoffment decrees have not been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Citing a stellar anomaly, he also said, "The imperial house flourishes in its root and branches, yet beyond the Prince of Ding no enfeoffment decrees have been issued.

sentences.zh: 望擇賢者，用唐故事，增廣嗣王、郡王之封，以慰祖宗意。」

translations.literal: I hope worthy men will be chosen, using Tang precedent, to broaden enfeoffments of heir princes and commandery princes, to comfort the ancestors' intent."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that worthy men be chosen, following Tang precedent, to broaden the enfeoffment of heir princes and commandery princes and thereby satisfy the intent of our ancestors."

sentences.zh: 時下詔蜀中，選優人補教坊，隨以為賤工不足辱詔書。

translations.literal: At the time an edict went down to Shu to select actors to fill the Music Bureau; Sui held that base craftsmen were not worth debasing an edict.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict went out to Shu to recruit actors for the Music Bureau, Sui protested that such base craftsmen were unworthy of an imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 又劾奏江、淮發運使鍾離瑾載奇花怪石數十艘，納禁中及賂權貴。

translations.literal: He again impeached Jiang-Huai Transport Commissioner Zhongli Jin for loading several tens of ships with exotic flowers and strange stones, presenting them within the Forbidden City and bribing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He again impeached Jiang-Huai Transport Commissioner Zhongli Jin for shipping dozens of boatloads of exotic flowers and strange stones into the palace and using them to bribe powerful officials.

sentences.zh: 累疏論丁謂姦邪，不宜還之內地；

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized that Ding Wei was treacherous and wicked and ought not be returned to the interior;
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized that Ding Wei was treacherous and wicked and ought not be recalled to the interior;

sentences.zh: 胡則，謂之黨，既以罪出陳州，不當復進職。

translations.literal: Hu Ze, of Wei's faction, having been expelled to Chen Prefecture for his crimes, ought not again be advanced in office.
translations.idiomatic: and that Hu Ze, a member of Wei's faction, having been banished to Chen Prefecture for his crimes, ought not be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 王欽若既死，詔塑其像茅山，列於仙官。

translations.literal: After Wang Qinruo died, an edict ordered his image cast at Mount Mao and listed among the immortal officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Qinruo's death, an edict ordered his image cast at Mount Mao and enrolled among the immortal officials.

sentences.zh: 隨言：「欽若贓汙無忌憚，考其行，豈神仙耶？

translations.literal: Sui said: "Qinruo was corrupt and unscrupulous; considering his conduct, how could he be an immortal?
translations.idiomatic: Sui protested, "Qinruo was corrupt beyond all restraint. Judging by his conduct, how could he be deemed an immortal?

sentences.zh: 宜察其妄。」

translations.literal: His presumption ought to be examined."
translations.idiomatic: This presumption ought to be investigated."

sentences.zh: 又言：「李維以詞臣求換武職，非所以勵廉節。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Li Wei as a literary official seeks to exchange for a military post—this is not the way to encourage integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Li Wei, a literary official, seeks to exchange his post for a military commission. This is no way to encourage integrity."

sentences.zh: 前後所論甚眾。

translations.literal: Before and after, what he discussed was very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials on such matters were numerous.

sentences.zh: 帝既益習天下事，而太后猶未歸政，隨請軍國常務，專稟帝旨，又諫太后不宜數幸外家，太后不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor had increasingly mastered affairs of the realm, yet the empress dowager had still not returned government; Sui requested that routine military and state affairs be reported solely to the emperor's will, and also remonstrated that the empress dowager ought not frequently visit her natal family—the empress dowager was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew more familiar with affairs of state, the empress dowager still had not returned the regency. Sui urged that routine military and civil business be reported solely to the emperor, and remonstrated that the empress dowager ought not visit her natal family so often. The empress dowager was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會隨請外，出知濟州，改起居郎。

translations.literal: When Sui requested an outside post, he was sent out to administer Ji Prefecture and changed to Diary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui requested an outside appointment, he was sent out to administer Ji Prefecture and reassigned as Diary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷尚書刑部員外郎，入兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and entered the capital to concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and recalled to serve concurrently as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言：「比年庶官僥幸請託，或對見之際，涕泗祈恩，或績效甚微，衒鬻要賞。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In recent years lower officials have relied on luck and patronage; some at audience weep and beg for favor, others with very slight achievement boast and demand rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "In recent years lower officials have grown shameless in their patronage-seeking. Some weep and beg for favor at audience; others with trifling achievements parade their merits and demand rewards.

sentences.zh: 亦有藩翰之臣，位尊職重，表章不遜，請求靡厭。

translations.literal: There are also frontier ministers of high rank and heavy responsibility whose memorials are insubordinate and whose requests know no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier ministers of high rank submit insubordinate memorials and make requests without end.

sentences.zh: 按察之司，燕安顧望，以容奸為大體，以舉職為近名，以巧詐為賢，以恬退為拙。

translations.literal: The inspection offices rest at ease and look about, taking tolerating wickedness as the great principle, taking performing duty as near to fame-seeking, taking crafty deceit as worth, and taking quiet withdrawal as clumsiness.
translations.idiomatic: The inspection offices rest at ease and look the other way, treating tolerance of wrongdoing as statesmanship, dutiful enforcement as self-promotion, cunning deceit as talent, and honest restraint as incompetence.

sentences.zh: 以至貪殘者瀆於貨財，老疾者不知止足。

translations.literal: Thus the greedy and cruel are insolent over wealth, and the old and ill know no stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The greedy grow insolent in their pursuit of wealth, and the old and infirm refuse to step aside.

sentences.zh: 請行申儆之法。」

translations.literal: I request that warning and admonition methods be implemented."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that stern admonition and discipline be enforced."

sentences.zh: 朝廷為下詔戒中外。

translations.literal: The court thereupon issued an edict warning within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon issued an edict of warning to officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，權同判吏部流內銓，以長定格從事，吏不得為奸。

translations.literal: Before long he was acting judge of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Internal Appointments; he conducted affairs by the longevity regulations, and clerks could not commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed acting judge of the Bureau of Internal Appointments, where he enforced the longevity regulations so strictly that clerks could not commit fraud.

sentences.zh: 改三司鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，以病足痹，辭不能拜。

translations.literal: On an embassy to the Khitan, because his feet were afflicted with paralysis, he declined, unable to bow.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, his feet were paralyzed by illness and he was unable to perform the required bows.

sentences.zh: 及還，為有司劾奏，奪一官，出知信州，徙宜州，再遷工部郎中、知應天府。

translations.literal: When he returned, the authorities impeached and memorialized; one rank was stripped; he was sent out to administer Xin Prefecture, transferred to Yi Prefecture, and again promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works and administrator of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the authorities impeached him, stripped him of one rank, and sent him out to administer Xin Prefecture. He was later transferred to Yi Prefecture and eventually promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works and administrator of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部副使，改天章閣待制，不旬日卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Household Commissioner, changed to Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall, and died within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Household Commissioner and appointed Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall, but died within ten days.

sentences.zh: 隨與孔道輔、曹修古同時為言事官，皆以清直聞。

translations.literal: Sui, together with Kong Daofu and Cao Xiugu, served at the same time as remonstrating officials, all known for purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Sui served alongside Kong Daofu and Cao Xiugu as remonstrating officials at the same time; all three were known for their integrity.

sentences.zh: 隨臨事明銳敢行，在蜀，人號為「水晶燈籠」。

translations.literal: Sui in affairs was sharp and daring in action; in Shu people called him the "crystal lantern."
translations.idiomatic: Sui was sharp and fearless in action; in Shu he was nicknamed the Crystal Lantern.

sentences.zh: 初，使契丹還，會貶，而官收所得馬十五乘。

translations.literal: Earlier, when he returned from the Khitan embassy he happened to be demoted, and the authorities confiscated the fifteen horses he had obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his Khitan embassy he happened to be demoted, and the authorities confiscated the fifteen horses he had acquired.

sentences.zh: 既卒，帝憐其家貧，賜錢六十萬。

translations.literal: After he died, the emperor pitied his family's poverty and bestowed six hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor, pitying his family's poverty, granted them six hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 曹修古

translations.literal: Cao Xiugu
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiugu

sentences.zh: 曹修古，字述之，建州建安人。

translations.literal: Cao Xiugu, styled Shuzhi, was a native of Jian'an in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiugu, whose style was Shuzhi, was a native of Jian'an in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士起家，累遷秘書丞、同判饒州。

translations.literal: He began his career as a jinshi graduate, was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Assistant and concurrent judge of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a jinshi graduate and rose through successive appointments to Secretariat Assistant and concurrent judge of Rao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋綬薦其材，召還，以太常博士為監察御史。

translations.literal: Song Shou recommended his talent; he was recalled and appointed Investigating Censor from his post as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shou recommended his ability, and he was recalled to serve as Investigating Censor from his post as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 上四事，曰行法令、審故事、惜材力、辨忠邪，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: He submitted four matters: enforcing statutes, examining precedents, cherishing resources and labor, and distinguishing loyalty from wickedness—the language was very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted four proposals: enforce the statutes, examine precedents, conserve resources and labor, and distinguish loyalty from wickedness. His language was urgent and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「唐貞觀中，嘗下詔令致仕官班本品見任上，欲其知恥而勇退也。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "In Tang's Zhenguan era, an edict once ordered that retired officials rank by their original grade above incumbents, wishing them to know shame and retire boldly.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "In the Zhenguan era of Tang, an edict once required that retired officials take precedence in court ranking over incumbents of the same grade, the intent being to shame them into willing retirement.

sentences.zh: 比有年餘八十，尚任班行，心力既衰，官事何補。

translations.literal: Recently there are those over eighty still serving in the ranks; their mind and strength are already weakened—what do they add to official business?
translations.idiomatic: Yet today men over eighty still hold office in the ranks. Their minds and strength are spent—what service can they still render?

sentences.zh: 請下有司，敕文武官年及七十，上書自言，特與遷官致仕，仍從貞觀舊制，即宿德勳賢，自如故事。」

translations.literal: I request that the authorities be ordered to command civil and military officials who reach seventy to memorialize on their own behalf and be specially granted promotion in rank and retirement, still following the Zhenguan old system; as for those of long virtue and meritorious worth, let them follow precedent as before."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that civil and military officials who reach seventy be required to memorialize for retirement and be granted a final promotion in rank, following the Zhenguan precedent, while men of exceptional virtue and long service may be treated according to established custom."

sentences.zh: 因著為令。

translations.literal: This was therefore enacted as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 修古嘗偕三院御史十二人晨朝，將至朝堂，黃門二人行馬不避，嗬者止之，反為所詈。

translations.literal: Xiugu once accompanied twelve censors of the three bureaus to morning audience; as they were about to reach the court hall, two Yellow Gate attendants rode without yielding; the shouters stopped them and were in turn reviled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu once accompanied twelve censors of the three bureaus to morning audience. As they neared the court hall, two Yellow Gate attendants rode past without yielding. When the attendants called out to stop them, they were reviled in return.

sentences.zh: 修古奏：「前史稱，御史臺尊，則天子尊。

translations.literal: Xiugu memorialized: "Former histories say: when the Censorate is honored, the Son of Heaven is honored.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu memorialized, "Former histories declare that when the Censorate is honored, the Son of Heaven is honored.

sentences.zh: 故事，三院同行與知雜事同，今黃門侮慢若此，請付所司劾治。」

translations.literal: By precedent, when the three bureaus travel together they rank the same as the one in charge of miscellaneous affairs; now the Yellow Gate have been so insulting and contemptuous—I request they be handed to the appropriate office for impeachment and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, censors of the three bureaus traveling together rank equal to the Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs. Yet these Yellow Gate attendants have shown such contempt. I beg that they be handed over for impeachment and punishment."

sentences.zh: 帝聞，立命笞之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he immediately ordered them flogged.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor immediately ordered them flogged.

sentences.zh: 晏殊以笏擊人折齒。

translations.literal: Yan Shu struck a man with his tablet and broke his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu struck one of them with his court tablet and broke his teeth.

sentences.zh: 修古奏：「殊身任輔弼，百僚所法，而忿躁亡大臣體。

translations.literal: Xiugu memorialized: "Shu personally bears the post of chief assistant, the model for all officials, yet in anger and rashness he has lost the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu memorialized, "Shu holds the post of chief minister and ought to be the model for all officials, yet in his anger he has forfeited the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 古者，三公不按吏，先朝陳恕於中書榜人，即時罷黜。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Three Excellencies did not beat clerks; in the previous reign Chen Shu posted a man's name at the Secretariat and he was dismissed at once.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Three Excellencies did not strike subordinates. In the previous reign, when Chen Shu posted a man's name at the Secretariat, he was dismissed at once.

sentences.zh: 請正典刑，以允公議。」

translations.literal: I request proper statutory punishment to satisfy public discussion."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he receive the proper statutory punishment to satisfy public opinion."

sentences.zh: 司天監主簿苗舜臣等嘗言，土宿留參，太白晝見，詔日官同考定。

translations.literal: Director of the Astronomy Bureau Registrar Miao Shunchen and others once said that the Earth Lodging lingered in the Three Enclosures and the Great White appeared in daylight; an edict ordered the solar officials jointly to examine and determine.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Shunchen, registrar of the Directorate of Astronomy, and others reported that the Earth Lodging lingered in the Three Enclosures and that the planet Venus appeared in daylight. The throne ordered the court astronomers to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 及奏，以謂土宿留參，順不相犯；

translations.literal: When they memorialized, they held that the Earth Lodging lingering in the Three Enclosures was compliant and did not mutually offend;
translations.idiomatic: Their report held that the Earth Lodging's lingering in the Three Enclosures was harmonious and not inauspicious;

sentences.zh: 太白晝見，日未過午。

translations.literal: the Great White appearing in daylight occurred before the sun had passed noon.
translations.idiomatic: and that Venus's appearance in daylight had occurred before noon.

sentences.zh: 舜臣等坐妄言災變被罰。

translations.literal: Shunchen and others were punished for falsely speaking of calamities and changes.
translations.idiomatic: Shunchen and his colleagues were punished for speaking falsely about celestial portents.

sentences.zh: 修古奏言：「日官所定，希旨悅上，未足為信。

translations.literal: Xiugu memorialized: "What the solar officials determined curries favor and pleases superiors—it is not sufficient to be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu memorialized, "The astronomers' findings curry favor with the throne and cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 今罰舜臣等，其事甚小，然恐人人自此畏避，佞媚取容，以災為福，天變不告，所損至大。」

translations.literal: Now punishing Shunchen and others—the matter is very small, yet I fear that from this everyone will shrink back in fear, fawn and flatter to gain favor, turn calamity into blessing, and not report heavenly changes—the harm will be very great."
translations.idiomatic: Punishing Shunchen may seem a small matter, yet I fear that hereafter everyone will shrink from speaking truth, fawning on superiors and turning calamity into blessing by concealing heavenly warnings. The harm would be immense."

sentences.zh: 禁中以翡翠羽為服玩，詔市於南越。

translations.literal: Within the Forbidden City kingfisher feathers were used for dress and ornaments; an edict ordered them purchased in southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace kingfisher feathers were used for dress and ornaments, and an edict ordered them purchased from southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 修古以謂重傷物命，且真宗時嘗禁采狨毛，故事未遠。

translations.literal: Xiugu held that this gravely harmed living creatures, and moreover in Emperor Zhenzong's time the gathering of macaque fur had been forbidden—the precedent was not distant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu protested that this wantonly destroyed life, and noted that Emperor Zhenzong had once forbidden the gathering of macaque fur—a precedent not long past.

sentences.zh: 命罷之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The order was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 時頗崇建塔廟，議營金閣，費不可勝計，修古極陳其不可。

translations.literal: At the time tower temples were greatly promoted; there was discussion of building a golden pavilion at incalculable expense; Xiugu urgently stated that it was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court greatly favored building pagodas and temples, and a golden pavilion was proposed at incalculable expense. Xiugu argued strenuously against it.

sentences.zh: 久之，出知歙州，徙南劍州，復為開封府判官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was sent out to administer She Prefecture, transferred to Nanjian Prefecture, and again served as Kaifeng judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out to administer She Prefecture, transferred to Nanjian Prefecture, and later reappointed judicial commissioner of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中侍御史，擢尚書刑部員外郎、知雜司事、權同判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He passed through Palace Attendant Censor, was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, in charge of miscellaneous bureau affairs, and acting judge of the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Internal Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant Censor and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, and acting judge of the Bureau of Internal Appointments.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，會太后兄子劉從德死，錄其姻戚至於廝役幾八十人，龍圖閣直學士馬季良、集賢校理錢曖，皆緣遺奏超授官秩，修古與楊偕、郭勸、段少連交章論列。

translations.literal: Within a month, when the empress dowager's elder brother's son Liu Congde died, nearly eighty in-laws down to menial servants were enrolled; Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Ma Jiliang and Hall of Assembled Talents Collator Qian Ai were all through his final memorial granted extraordinary ranks; Xiugu together with Yang Xie, Guo Quan, and Duan Shaolian submitted successive memorials discussing and arraying the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the empress dowager's nephew Liu Congde died. Nearly eighty relatives and servants were enrolled for preferment; Dragon Diagram Hall Academician Ma Jiliang and Hall of Assembled Talents Collator Qian Ai were among those promoted through his final memorial. Xiugu, together with Yang Xie, Guo Quan, and Duan Shaolian, submitted successive memorials protesting the appointments.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，下其章中書。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and sent their memorials down to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was enraged and referred their memorials to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大臣請黜修古知衢州，餘以次貶。

translations.literal: The great ministers requested that Xiugu be demoted to administer Qu Prefecture and the rest demoted in order.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers recommended demoting Xiugu to administer Qu Prefecture and the others in descending order.

sentences.zh: 太后以為責輕，命皆削一官，以修古為工部員外郎、同判杭州，未行，改知興化軍。

translations.literal: The empress dowager thought the punishment light and ordered all to be stripped of one rank; Xiugu was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and concurrent judge of Hangzhou, but before departing was changed to administrator of Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager deemed the punishment too light and ordered each man stripped of one rank. Xiugu was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and concurrent judge of Hangzhou, but before he could depart was reassigned to administer Xinghua Army.

sentences.zh: 會赦復官，卒。

translations.literal: When an amnesty restored his rank, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty restored his rank, he died.

sentences.zh: 修古立朝，慷慨有風節。

translations.literal: Xiugu in court was impassioned and had moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu served at court with passionate integrity.

sentences.zh: 當太后臨朝，權幸用事，人人顧望畏忌，而修古遇事輒言，無所回撓。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager held court, favorites wielded power; everyone looked about in fear, yet Xiugu on encountering affairs always spoke without any yielding.
translations.idiomatic: While the empress dowager held court and favorites wielded power, others looked on in fear, but Xiugu spoke out on every issue without yielding.

sentences.zh: 既沒，人多惜之。

translations.literal: After he died, many regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death many mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 家貧，不能歸葬，賓佐賻錢五十萬。

translations.literal: His family was poor and could not return his body for burial; guests and subordinates contributed five hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: His family was too poor to return his body for burial; colleagues contributed five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 季女泣白其母曰：「奈何以是累吾先人也。」

translations.literal: His youngest daughter wept and told her mother: "How can we burden our departed father with this?"
translations.idiomatic: His youngest daughter wept and told her mother, "How can we burden our departed father with this?"

sentences.zh: 卒拒不納。

translations.literal: In the end she refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she refused to accept the money.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，帝思修古忠，特贈右諫議大夫，賜其家錢二十萬，錄其婿劉勳為試將作監主簿。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, the emperor recalled Xiugu's loyalty and specially posthumously granted him Right Remonstrating Grand Master, bestowed his family two hundred thousand in cash, and enrolled his son-in-law Liu Xun as probationary Master of Works Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death the emperor recalled Xiugu's loyalty, posthumously granted him the rank of Right Remonstrating Grand Master, bestowed two hundred thousand cash on his family, and enrolled his son-in-law Liu Xun as probationary Master of Works Registrar.

sentences.zh: 修古無子，以兄子覲為後。

translations.literal: Xiugu had no son and took his elder brother's son Jin as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xiugu had no son and adopted his elder brother's son Jin as his heir.

sentences.zh: 覲知封州，儂智高亂，死之，見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: Jin administered Feng Prefecture; when Nong Zhigao rebelled, he died in the cause—see the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jin served as administrator of Feng Prefecture and died when Nong Zhigao rebelled; his biography appears in the Loyalty and Righteousness section.

sentences.zh: 弟修睦，性廉介自立，與修古同時舉進士，有聲鄉里，累官尚書都官員外郎、知邵武軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiumu was by nature pure, upright, and self-reliant; he passed the jinshi at the same time as Xiugu, had renown in his home district, and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice's Bureau of Punishments and administrator of Shaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiumu was pure and self-reliant by nature. He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Xiugu, won renown in their home district, and rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and administrator of Shaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞杜衍薦以為侍御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan recommended him as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan recommended him for appointment as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改司封員外郎，出知壽州，徙泉州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Seals, sent out to administer Shou Prefecture, and transferred to Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Seals, sent out to administer Shou Prefecture, and later transferred to Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐失舉，奪一官罷去。

translations.literal: Because of a failed recommendation he was stripped of one rank and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for a failed recommendation, stripped of one rank, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後以知吉州，不行，上書請老，不聽，分司南京，未幾致仕，年五十一。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed to administer Ji Prefecture but did not go; he memorialized requesting retirement, was not heard, served as commissioner at the Southern Capital, and before long retired at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed to administer Ji Prefecture but declined to go, memorialized for retirement without success, served as commissioner at the Southern Capital, and retired at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 章得象表其高，詔還所奪官，卒。

translations.literal: Zhang Dexiang memorialized his loftiness; an edict restored the rank that had been taken; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang memorialized his virtue; the throne restored his stripped rank, and he died.

sentences.zh: 曹氏自修古以直諒聞，其女子亦能不累於利，至覲，又能死其官，而修睦亦恬於仕進，不待老而歸，世以是賢之。

translations.literal: The Cao clan from Xiugu onward was known for straightforward integrity; its women also could avoid being burdened by profit; as for Jin, he could also die for his office; and Xiumu was content with official advancement, returning home without waiting for old age—the age therefore deemed them worthy.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiugu onward the Cao clan was known for integrity. Its women refused to be tainted by profit; Jin died in office; and Xiumu, content to withdraw from advancement, retired before old age. The age held them all in esteem.

sentences.zh: 郭勸，字仲褒，鄆州須城人。

translations.literal: Guo Quan, styled Zhongbao, was a native of Xucheng in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan, whose style was Zhongbao, was a native of Xucheng in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授寧化軍判官，累遷太常博士、通判密州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed judicial aide of Ninghua Army, and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and transit commissioner of Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as judicial aide of Ninghua Army and rose through successive appointments to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and transit commissioner of Mi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 特遷尚書屯田員外郎、梓州路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was specially transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Bureau of State Farms and transport judge of the Zizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of State Farms and transport judge of the Zizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 以母老固辭，復為博士、通判萊州。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he firmly declined and again became erudite and transit commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his mother's advanced age, he firmly declined and returned to serve as erudite and transit commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 州民霍亮為仇人誣罪死，吏受賕傅致之，勸為辨理得免。

translations.literal: A prefectural commoner Huo Liang was by an enemy falsely accused and sentenced to death; clerks took bribes and helped bring it about; Quan argued the case and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner named Huo Liang was falsely accused by an enemy and sentenced to death through bribery of the clerks, Quan argued his case and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 時宋綬出知應天府，杜衍在荊南，勸言綬有辭學，衍清直，不宜處外。

translations.literal: At the time Song Shou was sent out to administer Yingtian Prefecture and Du Yan was in Jingnan; Quan said Shou had literary learning and Yan was pure and upright—they ought not be placed outside.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Song Shou had been sent out to administer Yingtian Prefecture and Du Yan was posted to Jingnan. Quan argued that Shou possessed literary learning and Yan was upright—they ought not be kept from court.

sentences.zh: 又言：武勝軍節度使錢惟演遷延不赴陳州，覬望相位；

translations.literal: He also said: Military Commissioner of Wusheng Army Qian Weiyan delayed and did not proceed to Chen Prefecture, coveting the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: He also protested that Qian Weiyan, military commissioner of the Wusheng Army, delayed proceeding to Chen Prefecture while coveting the chancellorship;

sentences.zh: 弟惟濟任觀察使、定州總管，自請就遷留後；

translations.literal: his younger brother Weiji served as observation commissioner and overall commander of Ding Prefecture and requested transfer to remain in the rear;
