translations.idiomatic: that his brother Weiji, serving as observation commissioner and overall commander of Ding Prefecture, had requested transfer to remain in the rear;

sentences.zh: 胡則以罪罷三司使，乃遷工部侍郎、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: Hu Ze was removed as Three Departments Commissioner for his crimes yet was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: and that Hu Ze, removed as Three Departments Commissioner for his crimes, had nevertheless been promoted to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 請趣惟演上道，罷惟濟兵權，追則除命。

translations.literal: He requested that Weiyan be urged onto the road, Weiji's military authority be ended, and Ze's appointment order be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Weiyan be compelled to depart, Weiji's military authority be revoked, and Ze's appointment be rescinded.

sentences.zh: 又論劉從德遺奏恩濫，貶太常博士、監濰州稅。

translations.literal: He again discussed the excessive favor in Liu Congde's final memorial and was demoted to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and supervisor of Weizhou taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He again protested the excessive favor shown in Liu Congde's final memorial and was demoted to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and supervisor of Weizhou taxes.

sentences.zh: 改祠部員外郎、知萊州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Temples and administered Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Temples and appointed administrator of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，復為侍御史、判三司鹽鐵勾院。

translations.literal: After more than a month he again became Attending Censor and judged the Three Departments Salt and Iron Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he was restored as Attending Censor and assigned to judge the Three Departments Salt and Iron Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 郭皇后廢，議選納陳氏，勸進諫曰：「正家以正天下，自后妃始。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo was deposed and there was discussion of selecting and installing the Chen clan, Quan advanced remonstrance: "To rectify the family is to rectify the realm—it begins with the empress and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Guo was deposed and the court debated installing a woman of the Chen clan, Quan remonstrated, "To set the family in order is to set the realm in order, and that begins with the empress.

sentences.zh: 郭氏非有大故，不當廢。

translations.literal: The Guo clan has no great fault and ought not be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Guo empress has committed no grave offense and must not be deposed.

sentences.zh: 陳氏非世閥，不可以儷宸極。」

translations.literal: The Chen clan is not of an eminent house and cannot be matched to the imperial pinnacle."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen clan is not of an eminent house and cannot be elevated to the throne."

sentences.zh: 疏入，后已廢，而陳氏議遂寢。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the empress had already been deposed, but the Chen proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: By the time his memorial arrived the empress had already been deposed, but the proposal to install the Chen clan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎兼起居舍人、同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of War while also serving as Diary Attendant and Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War while concurrently serving as Diary Attendant and Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 馬季良自貶所求致仕，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Ma Jiliang from his place of demotion requested retirement and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jiliang, from his place of demotion, requested retirement, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 勸言：「致仕所以待賢者，豈負罪貶黜之人可得，請追還敕誥。」

translations.literal: Quan said: "Retirement is meant to treat the worthy—how can one who bears guilt and was demoted obtain it? I request that the edict and patent be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: Quan protested, "Retirement is reserved for the worthy. How can a man demoted for his crimes receive it? I beg that his edict of appointment be revoked."

sentences.zh: 又言：「發運使劉承德獻輪扇浴器，大率以媚上也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Transport Commissioner Liu Chengde presented wheel-fans and bathing vessels—mostly to flatter superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Transport Commissioner Liu Chengde presented wheel-fans and bathing vessels—gifts meant chiefly to flatter the throne.

sentences.zh: 請付外毀，以戒邪佞。」

translations.literal: I request they be handed outside and destroyed to warn the wicked and fawning."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they be destroyed publicly as a warning to sycophants."

sentences.zh: 趙元昊襲父位，以勸為官告使，所遺百萬，悉拒不受。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao succeeded his father, Quan was made patent envoy; the million in gifts presented he entirely refused.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yuanhao succeeded his father, Quan served as patent envoy and refused every gift of the million offered him.

sentences.zh: 還，兼侍御史知雜事、權判流內銓，遷工部郎中、度支副使，拜天章閣待制、知延州。

translations.literal: On return he concurrently served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs and acting judge of the Bureau of Internal Appointments, was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Works and Vice Commissioner of the Treasury, and was appointed Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall and administrator of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs and acting judge of the Bureau of Internal Appointments, was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works and Vice Commissioner of the Treasury, and appointed Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall and administrator of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊將山遇率其族來歸，且言元昊將反。

translations.literal: Yuanhao's general Shanyu led his clan to submit and also said Yuanhao would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao's general Shanyu led his clan to defect and reported that Yuanhao was about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 勸與兵馬鈐轄李渭議，自德明納貢四十年，有內附者未嘗留，乃奏卻之。

translations.literal: Quan discussed with Military Affairs Commissioner Li Wei that since Deming began tribute forty years ago, those who submitted inward had never been retained, and memorialized to send them back.
translations.idiomatic: Quan consulted Military Affairs Commissioner Li Wei and noted that in the forty years since Deming began paying tribute, defectors had never been retained. He memorialized to send Shanyu back.

sentences.zh: 是冬，元昊果反，遣其使稱偽官來。

translations.literal: That winter Yuanhao indeed rebelled and sent his envoy bearing false titles.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yuanhao did rebel and sent an envoy bearing titles of his new regime.

sentences.zh: 勸視其表函猶稱臣，因上奏曰：「元昊雖僭中國名號，然尚稱臣，可漸以禮屈之，願與大臣熟議。」

translations.literal: Quan saw that the cover of his memorial still styled him subject and therefore memorialized: "Although Yuanhao has usurped China's titles, he still calls himself subject; he may gradually be bent by ritual—I wish to deliberate thoroughly with the great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Quan observed that the envoy's documents still addressed him as a subject and memorialized, "Although Yuanhao has usurped imperial titles, he still calls himself a subject. He may yet be brought to heel through ritual propriety. I beg to deliberate this thoroughly with the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 遂落職知齊州，改淄州，數月，移磁州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon demoted in office to administer Qi Prefecture, changed to Zi Prefecture, and after several months transferred to Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to administer Qi Prefecture, transferred to Zi Prefecture, and after several months moved to Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元昊益侵邊，關陝擾攘，言者猶指勸不當絕山遇事，又降兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Yuanhao increasingly raided the border and Guan and Shaan were disturbed; critics still pointed to Quan's error in rejecting Shanyu, and he was again demoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanhao intensified his border raids and the Guan-Shaan region fell into turmoil, critics still blamed Quan for rejecting Shanyu, and he was demoted again to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復，知鳳翔府，尋復待制。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he was recalled from mourning, administered Fengxiang Prefecture, and soon restored as Gentleman in Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to administer Fengxiang Prefecture and soon restored to Gentleman in Waiting.

sentences.zh: 召權戶部副使，以龍圖閣直學士知滑州，再遷兵部郎中，徙滄州，又徙成德軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as acting Vice Household Commissioner, made Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and administrator of Hua Prefecture, again promoted to Director in the Ministry of War, transferred to Cang Prefecture, and again to Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as acting Vice Household Commissioner, appointed Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and administrator of Hua Prefecture, promoted again to Director in the Ministry of War, transferred to Cang Prefecture, and then to Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 盜起甘陵，徙鄆州。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Ganling; he was transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Ganling he was transferred to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而知成德軍韓琦言，勸所遣將張忠、劉遵，平賊功皆第一，特詔獎諭。

translations.literal: Before long Han Qi of Chengde Army reported that the generals Quan had dispatched, Zhang Zhong and Liu Zun, ranked first in merit for pacifying the bandits; a special edict commended and instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi of Chengde Army soon reported that the generals Quan had dispatched, Zhang Zhong and Liu Zun, had ranked first in merit for suppressing the bandits. A special edict commended Quan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為翰林侍讀學士，復判流內銓，改左諫議大夫、權御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, again judged the Bureau of Internal Appointments, and was changed to Left Remonstrating Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician, again assigned to judge the Bureau of Internal Appointments, and promoted to Left Remonstrating Grand Master and acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，辭不受，而請贈其祖萊陽令寧，遂以為尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief of the Palace Secretariat, declined and did not accept, but requested posthumous grant for his grandfather Ning, magistrate of Laiyang, and was therefore made Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites' Bureau of Temples.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered promotion to Attendant-in-Chief but declined, requesting instead a posthumous grant for his grandfather Ning, former magistrate of Laiyang, which was granted as Vice Director in the Bureau of Temples.

sentences.zh: 衛士有相惡者，陰置刃衣篋中，從勾當皇城司楊景宗入禁門，既而為閽者所得，景宗輒隱不以聞。

translations.literal: Among the guards were men who hated each other; one secretly placed a blade in his clothing chest and followed Commissioner of the Imperial City Yang Jingzong through the forbidden gate; he was then seized by the gatekeepers, but Jingzong concealed it and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: Among the palace guards two men bore a grudge; one hid a blade in his clothing and entered the forbidden precinct with Yang Jingzong, commissioner of the Imperial City. Gatekeepers seized him, but Jingzong concealed the incident and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 勸請先治景宗罪，章再上，不聽，又廷爭累日，卒貶景宗。

translations.literal: Quan requested that Jingzong's offense be punished first; the memorial was submitted again and not heard; he argued in court for many days, and in the end Jingzong was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Quan demanded that Jingzong be punished first. His memorial was ignored; he argued in open court for days, and Jingzong was finally demoted.

sentences.zh: 祀明堂，將加恩中外官，勸就齋次，帥群御史求對，不許，又極論之。

translations.literal: When sacrificing at the Bright Hall, as favors were to be extended to officials within and without, Quan went to the fasting station, led the censors to seek audience, was not permitted, and again argued to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bright Hall sacrifice, as the court prepared to extend favors to officials throughout the realm, Quan went to the fasting station and led the censors to demand audience. When refused, he argued strenuously in court.

sentences.zh: 是年，復為侍讀學士、同知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: That year he again became Reader Academician and Associate Director of the Memorial Gateway and Silver Terrace Office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was again appointed Reader Academician and Associate Director of the Memorial Gateway and Silver Terrace Office.

sentences.zh: 勸性廉儉，居無長物。

translations.literal: Quan was by nature pure and frugal; in his dwelling there were no surplus things.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was pure and frugal by nature and kept nothing superfluous in his home.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂諸子曰：「顏魯公云：『生得五品服章紱，任子為齋郎，足矣。』」

translations.literal: He once told his sons: "Yan the Duke of Lu said: 'In life to obtain fifth-rank robes, seals, and ribbons, and to have one's son appointed a Fast Officer—that is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: He once told his sons, "Yan the Duke of Lu said, 'To attain fifth-rank robes and insignia in life, and to secure one's son an appointment as Fast Officer—that is enough.'

sentences.zh: 及再為侍讀，曰：「吾起諸生，志不過郡守，今年七十，列侍從，可以歸矣。」

translations.literal: When he again became Attendant Reader he said: "I rose from a common scholar; my ambition did not exceed prefectural administrator; this year I am seventy, ranked among the attendants—it is time to return."
translations.idiomatic: When he again became Attendant Reader he said, "I rose from the ranks of scholars with no ambition beyond a prefecture. At seventy I stand among the emperor's attendants. It is time to go home."

sentences.zh: 遂用元日拜章，三上不得謝，賜銀使市田宅。

translations.literal: He thereupon on New Year's Day submitted a memorial; three times he submitted without being granted leave; silver was bestowed for him to purchase fields and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day he submitted his resignation three times without success. The throne granted him silver to purchase fields and a residence.

sentences.zh: 後二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died two years later.

sentences.zh: 子源明，治平中，為太常博士。

translations.literal: His son Yuanming, in the Zhiping era, served as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanming served as Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple during the Zhiping era.

sentences.zh: 會御史知雜事呂誨等奏彈中書議追崇濮安懿王典禮非是，被黜，以源明補監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: When Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs Lü Hui and others memorialized impeaching the Secretariat's proposal to posthumously honor Prince Anyi of Pu as incorrect in ritual, they were dismissed and Yuanming was appointed to fill Investigating Censor in probation.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Hui and other censors memorialized against the Secretariat's proposal to posthumously honor Prince Anyi of Pu, they were dismissed and Yuanming was appointed probationary Investigating Censor in their place.

sentences.zh: 源明乞免除命，請追誨等，遂聽免。

translations.literal: Yuanming begged to be relieved of the appointment and requested recall of Hui and the others; he was then permitted to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming begged to be relieved of the appointment and asked that Hui and the others be recalled. His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 後以職方員外郎知單州，卒。

translations.literal: Later as Vice Director in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Appointments he administered Shan Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments and administrator of Shan Prefecture, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 段少連

translations.literal: Duan Shaolian
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shaolian

sentences.zh: 段少連，字希逸，開封人。

translations.literal: Duan Shaolian, styled Xiyi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shaolian, whose style was Xiyi, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 其母嘗夢鳳集家庭，寤而生少連。

translations.literal: His mother once dreamed that a phoenix gathered in the family courtyard; on waking she gave birth to Shaolian.
translations.idiomatic: His mother once dreamed that a phoenix alighted in the family courtyard; on waking she gave birth to Shaolian.

sentences.zh: 及長，美姿表，倜儻有識度。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had a handsome appearance and was free-spirited with discernment.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew to manhood he was handsome in bearing, free-spirited, and possessed of sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 舉服勤詞學，為試秘書省校書郎、知崇陽縣。

translations.literal: He passed the Diligent Literary Examination, was tried as collator of the Secretariat, and administered Chongyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Diligent Literary Examination, served as collator of the Secretariat on probation, and was appointed magistrate of Chongyang County.

sentences.zh: 崇陽劇邑，自張詠為令有治狀，其後惟少連能繼其風跡。

translations.literal: Chongyang was a difficult county; since Zhang Yong as magistrate had shown good governance, afterward only Shaolian could continue his manner and traces.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyang was a difficult county. Since Zhang Yong's tenure as magistrate, only Shaolian had matched his record of capable governance.

sentences.zh: 權杭州觀察判官。

translations.literal: He acted as Hangzhou observation commissioner judge.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting judge under the Hangzhou observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 預校《道經》，改秘書省著作佐郎，歷知蒙城、名山、金華三縣，以本省丞為審刑院詳議官。

translations.literal: He participated in collating the Classic of the Way, was changed to Secretariat Drafting Assistant, successively administered Mengcheng, Mingshan, and Jinhua counties, and from assistant in his home bureau became detailed deliberation officer of the Court for Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He helped collate the Classic of the Way, was appointed Secretariat Drafting Assistant, served in succession as magistrate of Mengcheng, Mingshan, and Jinhua counties, and was then made detailed deliberation officer of the Court for Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 張士遜守江寧，辟通判府事，還為御史臺推直官，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shisun guarded Jiangning he recruited him as transit commissioner of prefectural affairs; on return he became investigating officer of the Censorate and was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shisun was posted to Jiangning he recruited Shaolian as transit commissioner. On returning to the capital he served as investigating officer in the Censorate and was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 論劉從德遺奏恩濫，降秘書丞、監漣水軍酒稅。

translations.literal: For discussing the excessive favor in Liu Congde's final memorial he was demoted to Secretariat Assistant and supervisor of Lianshui Army wine taxes.
translations.idiomatic: For protesting the excessive favor shown in Liu Congde's final memorial he was demoted to Secretariat Assistant and supervisor of Lianshui Army wine taxes.

sentences.zh: 復為博士、通判天雄軍。

translations.literal: He again became erudite and transit commissioner of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored as erudite and transit commissioner of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，召為殿中侍御史，與孔道輔等伏閣言郭皇后不當廢，少連坐贖。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died he was summoned as Palace Attendant Censor; with Kong Daofu and others he prostrated at the gate saying Empress Guo ought not be deposed; Shaolian was punished by fine.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager's death he was summoned as Palace Attendant Censor. With Kong Daofu and others he blocked the gate to protest the deposition of Empress Guo and was fined.

sentences.zh: 復上疏曰：「陛下親政以來，進用直臣，開辟言路，天下無不歡欣。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Since Your Majesty personally took government, upright ministers have been advanced and the path of speech opened—throughout the realm none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again, "Since Your Majesty assumed personal rule, upright ministers have been promoted and the path of remonstrance opened. The realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 一旦以諫官、御史伏閣，遽行黜責，中外皆以為非陛下意。

translations.literal: In a single day because remonstrators and censors prostrated at the gate, dismissal and punishment were hastily carried out—within and without all thought this was not Your Majesty's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a single day, because remonstrators and censors blocked the gate, they were hastily dismissed and punished. Court and country alike believed this was not Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 蓋執政大臣，假天威以出道輔、仲淹，而斷來者之說也。

translations.literal: It was rather the chief ministers who borrowed heaven's authority to drive out Daofu and Zhongyan and cut off the speech of those who would come after.
translations.idiomatic: Surely the chief ministers borrowed imperial authority to drive out Daofu and Fan Zhongyan and to silence those who would speak after them.

sentences.zh: 竊睹戒諭：『自今有章，宜如故事密上，毋得群詣殿門請對。』

translations.literal: I have seen the admonition: 'From now on when there are memorials, they should as precedent be submitted in secret; one must not in groups go to the hall gate to request audience.'
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the admonition: 'Hereafter memorials must be submitted in secret as of old; groups must not come to the hall gate to demand audience.'

sentences.zh: 且伏閣上疏，豈非故事，今遽絕之，則國家復有大事，誰敢旅進而言者。

translations.literal: Yet prostrating at the gate to submit memorials—is this not precedent? If it is now abruptly ended, then when the state again has great affairs, who will dare advance in company to speak?
translations.idiomatic: Yet blocking the gate to submit memorials is itself precedent. If this is now forbidden, who will dare speak out when the state faces grave matters?

sentences.zh: 昔唐陽城王仲舒伏閣雪陸贄，崔元亮叩殿陛理宋申錫，前史以為美事。

translations.literal: Formerly in Tang, Yang Cheng and Wang Zhongshu prostrated at the gate to clear Lu Zhi; Cui Yuanliang knocked on the hall steps to vindicate Song Shenxi—the former histories deemed these fine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times Yang Cheng and Wang Zhongshu blocked the gate to vindicate Lu Zhi, and Cui Yuanliang knocked on the hall steps to defend Song Shenxi—acts the histories praise.

sentences.zh: 今陛下未忍廢黜皇后，而兩府列狀議降為妃，諫官、御史，安敢緘默。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has not yet borne to depose and dismiss the empress, yet the Two Departments array documents discussing demotion to consort—how can remonstrators and censors dare be silent?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has not yet resolved to depose the empress, yet the Two Departments have memorialized to reduce her to consort. How can remonstrators and censors remain silent?

sentences.zh: 陛下深惟道輔等所言為阿黨乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty deeply consider whether what Daofu and the others said was faction?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty truly believe that Daofu and his colleagues spoke as a faction?

sentences.zh: 為忠亮乎？」

translations.literal: Or loyalty and candor?
translations.idiomatic: Or as loyal and candid men?"

sentences.zh: 疏入不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：

translations.literal: He again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 「高明粹清，凝德無累者，天之道也。

translations.literal: "Lofty brightness, pure clarity, and virtue concentrated without encumbrance—this is heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: "Lofty, pure, and clear—virtue concentrated without blemish—is the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 氛祲蔽翳，晦明偶差，乃陰陽之沴爾。

translations.literal: Malign vapors veiling and shading, dark and bright occasionally diverging—these are merely yin and yang's injuries.
translations.idiomatic: When malign vapors obscure the light and yin and yang fall out of balance, these are merely disturbances in the cosmic order.

sentences.zh: 象天德者，君之體也。

translations.literal: To embody heaven's virtue is the ruler's substance.
translations.idiomatic: To embody the virtue of Heaven is the substance of rulership.

sentences.zh: 治陰陽者，臣之職也。

translations.literal: To regulate yin and yang is the minister's duty.
translations.idiomatic: To regulate yin and yang is the minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 陛下秉一德、臨萬方，有生之類，莫不浸涵德澤。

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds to one virtue and faces the ten thousand regions; all that live are steeped in virtuous favor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds to single-hearted virtue and rules the ten thousand regions; every living thing is steeped in your gracious favor.

sentences.zh: 而氛祲蔽翳，偶差晦明，以累聖德者，由大臣懷祿而不諫，小臣畏罪而不言。

translations.literal: Yet malign vapors veil and shade, occasionally skewing dark and bright and burdening sagely virtue—this is because great ministers cling to salary and do not remonstrate, and lesser ministers fear punishment and do not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when malign influences obscure the light and burden your sagely virtue, it is because great ministers cling to their salaries and will not remonstrate, and lesser ministers fear punishment and will not speak.

sentences.zh: 臣獨何人，敢貢狂瞽。

translations.literal: What sort of person am I alone, that I dare offer reckless blindness?
translations.idiomatic: Who am I to offer such reckless counsel?

sentences.zh: 竊痛陛下履仁聖之具美，乏骨鯁之良輔，因成不忍之忿，又稽不遠之復。

translations.literal: I grieve that Your Majesty treads the full beauty of benevolence and sagacity yet lacks bone-in-the-throat worthy assistants, thereby forming an unenduring anger and also delaying the not-distant return.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that Your Majesty embodies the fullness of benevolence and sagacity yet lacks forthright assistants, and that anger born of forbearance has led you to neglect timely correction.

sentences.zh: 臣是以瀝肝膽，披情愫，為陛下廓清氛祲蔽翳之累。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore pours out liver and gall, lays bare true feeling, and for Your Majesty clears away the burden of malign vapors veiling and shading.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore pour out my heart and lay bare my true feelings, that Your Majesty may clear away these obscuring influences.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『夫夫婦婦而家道正，正家而天下定。』

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'When husband is husband and wife is wife, the family Way is correct; when the family is corrected, the realm is settled.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'When husband and wife each fulfill their roles, the family Way is set right; when the family is set right, the realm is settled.'

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『刑于寡妻，以御于家邦。』

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Take as model to the primary wife, thereby to govern family and state.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'Set an example for your primary wife, and thereby govern family and state.'

sentences.zh: 若然，則君天下修化本者，莫不自內而刑外也。

translations.literal: If so, then one who rules the realm and cultivates the root of transformation does so by disciplining outward from within.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one who rules the realm and cultivates the root of moral transformation must begin within and extend outward.

sentences.zh: 況聞入道降妃之議，出自臣下。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear that the proposal to enter the Way and demote to consort came from subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I hear that the proposal to have the empress take the tonsure and be reduced to consort originated among your ministers.

sentences.zh: 且后妃有罪，黜出告宗廟，廢則為庶人，安有不示之於天下，不告之於祖宗，而陰行臣下之議乎？

translations.literal: When an empress or consort has guilt, she is dismissed and the ancestral temple is informed; if deposed she becomes a commoner—how can there be not showing this to the realm, not informing the ancestors, yet secretly carrying out subordinates' proposals?
translations.idiomatic: When an empress is guilty she is dismissed with announcement to the ancestral temple; if deposed she becomes a commoner. How can such a matter be concealed from the realm and the ancestors while ministers' proposals are carried out in secret?

sentences.zh: 且皇后以小過降為妃，則臣下之婦有小過者，亦當降為妾矣。

translations.literal: If the empress for a small fault is demoted to consort, then officials' wives with small faults should also be demoted to concubines.
translations.idiomatic: If the empress is reduced to consort for a minor fault, then every official whose wife commits a minor fault must reduce her to concubine as well.

sentences.zh: 比抗章請對，不蒙賜召，豈非奸邪之臣，離間陛下耶？

translations.literal: Recently we resisted with memorials requesting audience and were not granted summons—is this not wicked ministers driving a wedge between Your Majesty and us?
translations.idiomatic: When we submitted memorials requesting audience and were not summoned, was this not the work of wicked ministers seeking to drive a wedge between Your Majesty and us?

sentences.zh: 臣等赴中書，時執政之臣，謂后有妒忌之行，始議入道，終降為妃。

translations.literal: When we went to the Secretariat, the ministers then in power said the empress had jealous conduct; at first they discussed entering the Way, and in the end demotion to consort.
translations.idiomatic: When we went to the Secretariat, the ministers in power said the empress had shown jealousy; they first proposed the tonsure and finally reduction to consort.

sentences.zh: 兼云有上封者，慮后不利於聖躬，故築高垣，置在別館。

translations.literal: They also said there were sealed memorials fearing the empress would harm the sacred person, and therefore built high walls and placed her in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: They also cited sealed memorials claiming that the empress might harm Your Majesty's person, and therefore had her walled within a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 臣等備言中外之議，以為未可。

translations.literal: We fully stated the discussions within and without and held that it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: We stated fully the views of court and country and held that the proposal was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 願速降明詔，復中宮位號，以安民心。

translations.literal: We wish that a clear edict be quickly issued to restore the Central Palace's title and rank, to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Your Majesty issue a clear edict at once restoring the empress's title and rank to reassure the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 翌日詔出，乃云『中宮有過，掖庭具知，特示涵容，未行遽黜，置之別館，俾自省修，供給之間，一切如故。』

translations.literal: The next day an edict issued, saying: 'The Central Palace has faults, the inner palace all know; special forbearance is shown, and she is not hastily deposed but placed in a separate lodge to reflect and reform; in provisions, all is as before.'
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict appeared, stating that the empress had faults known to the inner palace, that forbearance was shown by not hastily deposing her, that she was placed in a separate lodge for reflection, and that her provisions remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 臣未審黜置別館，為后為妃？

translations.literal: Your subjects do not yet ascertain whether placement in a separate lodge means empress or consort.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot tell whether placement in a separate lodge means she remains empress or has become consort.

sentences.zh: 詔書不言，安所取信。

translations.literal: The edict does not say—where is trust to be taken?
translations.idiomatic: The edict does not say, and there is nothing on which the realm may rely.

sentences.zh: 況皇后事陛下一紀有餘，而輔臣倉卒以降黜之議，惑於宸聽，搢紳循默，無敢為陛下言者。

translations.literal: Moreover the empress has served Your Majesty for more than twelve years, yet assistant ministers hastily proposed demotion, confusing imperial hearing; gentry and officials followed in silence, none daring to speak for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The empress has served Your Majesty for more than twelve years, yet chief ministers hastily proposed her demotion and confused your judgment. Officials throughout the court fell silent, none daring to speak for you.

sentences.zh: 臣所謂氛祲蔽翳，以累聖德者，蓋臣職有曠爾。

translations.literal: What your subject called malign vapors veiling and shading to burden sagely virtue—this is because ministerial duty was neglected.
translations.idiomatic: The malign influences I spoke of that burden your sagely virtue stem from our own failure in ministerial duty.

sentences.zh: 臣竊恐奸邪之人，引漢武幽陳皇后故事，以諂惑陛下。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that wicked men cite Emperor Wu of Han's seclusion of Empress Chen as precedent to flatter and mislead Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that wicked men cite Emperor Wu's seclusion of Empress Chen as precedent to flatter and mislead Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且漢武驕奢淫縱之主，固不足踵其行事。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Wu was a ruler of arrogance, luxury, and dissipation—his conduct is certainly not worth following.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute—a ruler whose conduct is certainly not worth emulating.

sentences.zh: 而為人臣者，思致君如堯、舜，豈致君如漢武哉！

translations.literal: Yet for one who is a subject, the thought is to bring the ruler to be like Yao and Shun—how could one bring the ruler to be like Emperor Wu!
translations.idiomatic: A subject ought to guide his ruler toward Yao and Shun. How could he guide him toward Emperor Wu!

sentences.zh: 今皇后置於別館，必恐懼修省，陛下仁恕之德，施於天下，而獨不加於中宮乎？

translations.literal: Now the empress is placed in a separate lodge and must fear and reflect; Your Majesty's benevolent and forgiving virtue is extended to the realm—will it alone not be extended to the Central Palace?
translations.idiomatic: The empress now sits in a separate lodge, surely in fear and reflection. Your benevolent and forgiving virtue extends throughout the realm—will it not extend to the empress?

sentences.zh: 願詔復中宮位號，杜絕非間，待之如初。

translations.literal: We wish an edict to restore the Central Palace's title and rank, cut off improper divisions, and treat her as at first.
translations.idiomatic: We beg an edict restoring her title and rank, cutting off all improper division, and treating her as before.

sentences.zh: 天地以正，陰陽以和，人神共歡，豈不美哉。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth would be set right, yin and yang harmonized, men and spirits rejoicing together—would it not be beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth would be set right, yin and yang harmonized, and men and spirits would rejoice together. What could be more beautiful?

sentences.zh: 陛下苟為邪臣所蔽，不加省察，臣恐高宗王后之枉，必見於他日，宮闈不正之亂，未測於將來，惟聖神慮焉。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is obscured by wicked ministers and does not examine and reflect, your subject fears the wrong done to Empress Wang under Emperor Gaozong will surely appear on another day, and disorder from an improper inner palace cannot be measured in the future—only the sage spirit should consider this."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty remains obscured by wicked ministers and does not reflect, I fear the injustice done to Empress Wang under Emperor Gaozong will be repeated, and disorder within the palace cannot be foreseen. Only Your Majesty's sage wisdom can prevent it."

sentences.zh: 未幾，除開封府判官，改尚書刑部員外郎、直集賢院，為三司度支判官，出為兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Kaifeng judicial commissioner, changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents, made Treasury Commissioner of the Three Departments, and sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed judicial commissioner of Kaifeng, promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents, made Treasury Commissioner of the Three Departments, and sent out as Vice Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 舊使者所至郡縣，索簿書，不暇殫閱，往往委之吏胥，吏胥持以為貨。

translations.literal: Former envoys at each prefecture and county they reached demanded account books, had no time to read them fully, and often entrusted them to clerks, who held them as merchandise.
translations.idiomatic: Former envoys at each prefecture and county demanded account books but had no time to read them thoroughly, often entrusting them to clerks who treated them as merchandise.

sentences.zh: 少連命郡縣上簿書悉緘識，遇事間指取一二自閱，摘其非是者按之，餘不及閱者，全緘識以還。

translations.literal: Shaolian ordered prefectures and counties to submit account books all sealed and marked; when affairs arose he would point and take one or two to read himself, pick out what was not correct and investigate, and what he did not reach to read was returned fully sealed and marked.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolian ordered all account books sealed on submission. When matters arose he would select one or two to read himself, investigate any irregularities, and return the rest still fully sealed.

sentences.zh: 由是吏不能為奸，而州縣簿書莫敢不治矣。

translations.literal: Thus clerks could not commit fraud, and prefectural and county account books none dared leave untended.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks could no longer commit fraud, and prefectural and county records were kept in proper order.

sentences.zh: 部吏有過，召詰曰：「聞子所為若此，有之乎？

translations.literal: When subordinates in his bureau had faults he summoned and questioned them: "I hear you have acted thus—is it so?
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate erred he summoned him and asked, "I hear you have acted thus. Is it true?

sentences.zh: 有當告我，我容汝自新；

translations.literal: If so you should tell me and I will allow you to renew yourself;
translations.idiomatic: If so, tell me and I will allow you to reform;

sentences.zh: 苟以為無，吾不使善人被謗，即為汝辨明矣。」

translations.literal: if you hold there is none, I will not let a good man be slandered and will at once clarify it for you."
translations.idiomatic: if you deny it, I will not let an honest man be slandered and will clear your name at once."

sentences.zh: 吏不敢欺，皆以實對。

translations.literal: Clerks did not dare deceive and all answered according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks did not dare deceive him and answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 少連每得其情，諄諄戒飭使去，後有能自改過者，猶保任之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shaolian got the facts he earnestly admonished and sent them away; afterward those who could reform themselves he still guaranteed and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the facts he admonished them earnestly and sent them away; those who later reformed themselves he still recommended for office.

sentences.zh: 秀州獄死無罪人，時少連在杭，吏畏恐聚謀，偽為死者服罪款，未及綴，屬少連已舟入城，訊獄吏，具服請罪，以為神明。

translations.literal: In Xiuzhou prison an innocent man died in custody; at the time Shaolian was in Hangzhou; clerks in fear gathered to plot and forged a confession for the dead man; before they could finish, Shaolian had already entered the city by boat; he questioned the prison clerks, who fully confessed and begged punishment, deeming him divine.
translations.idiomatic: When an innocent man died in Xiuzhou prison, the clerks in fear plotted to forge a confession. Before they could finish, Shaolian arrived in Hangzhou by boat, questioned the prison staff, and received their full confession. They took him for a divine judge.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄭向守杭，無治才。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Xiang guarded Hangzhou and lacked governing ability.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zheng Xiang held Hangzhou and lacked governing ability.

sentences.zh: 訟者不服，往往自州出，徑趨少連；

translations.literal: Litigants who were dissatisfied often left the prefecture and went straight to Shaolian;
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfied litigants often bypassed the prefecture and went straight to Shaolian;

sentences.zh: 少連一言處決，莫不盡其理。

translations.literal: Shaolian with a single word decided cases, none failing to reach full principle.
translations.idiomatic: and Shaolian settled each case with a single ruling that fully addressed its merits.

sentences.zh: 徙使淮南，兼發運司事，加兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred as envoy to Huainan, concurrently in charge of transport office affairs, and advanced to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as envoy to Huainan with concurrent charge of transport affairs and promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 又徙陝西。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉柴宗慶知陝州，縱其下撓民，少連入境，劾奏之。

translations.literal: Commandant-escort Chai Zongqing administered Shan Prefecture and indulged his subordinates in harassing the people; when Shaolian entered the circuit he impeached and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant-escort Chai Zongqing administered Shan Prefecture and allowed his subordinates to harass the people. When Shaolian entered the circuit he impeached him.

sentences.zh: 入兼侍御史知雜事，逾月，為三司度支副使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to concurrently serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs; after a month he became Vice Treasury Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to serve as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs and a month later became Vice Treasury Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 河東地震，奉使安撫。

translations.literal: When Hedong suffered an earthquake he was sent on a pacification mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong suffered an earthquake he was sent on a pacification mission.

sentences.zh: 還，擢工部郎中、天章閣待制、知廣州。

translations.literal: On return he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall, and administrator of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, Gentleman in Waiting at the Heavenly Writings Hall, and administrator of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時元昊反，范仲淹薦少連才堪將帥，遷龍圖閣直學士、知涇州，改渭州，命未至而卒。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanhao rebelled; Fan Zhongyan recommended that Shaolian's talent suited command of armies; he was transferred to Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and administrator of Jing Prefecture, changed to Wei Prefecture, and died before the appointment arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, Fan Zhongyan recommended Shaolian as capable of military command. He was appointed Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and administrator of Jing Prefecture, then transferred to Wei Prefecture, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 少連通敏有才，遇事無大小，決遣如流，不為權勢所屈。

translations.literal: Shaolian was penetrating, quick, and talented; in affairs great or small he decided and dispatched like flowing water and was not bent by power and influence.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolian was quick-witted and capable; in affairs great or small he decided and dispatched with ease and would not yield to power or influence.

sentences.zh: 既卒，仁宗歎惜之。

translations.literal: After he died, Emperor Renzong sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Emperor Renzong sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人有言：「山有猛獸，藜藿為之不采。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: The ancients had a saying: "When a mountain has fierce beasts, the wild greens are not picked for it."
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: The ancients observed, "When a mountain holds fierce beasts, no one picks the wild greens upon it."

sentences.zh: 當天聖、明道間，天子富於春秋，母后稱制，而內外肅然，紀綱具舉，朝政亡大闕失，奸人不得以自肆者，繇言路得人故也。

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng and Mingdao eras, the Son of Heaven was rich in youth, the empress dowager held regency, yet within and without were solemn, regulations were fully raised, court government had no great lapses, and wicked men could not indulge themselves—this was because the path of speech obtained worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng and Mingdao eras the emperor was young and the empress dowager held regency, yet within and without the court remained orderly, regulations were enforced, and no great lapse marred governance. Wicked men could not run riot because the path of remonstrance was staffed with worthy men.

sentences.zh: 是時，孔道輔、鞠詠、劉隨、曹修古迭為諫官、御史，郭勸、段少連繼之，皆侃侃正色，遇事輒言，被斥逐，不更其守。

translations.literal: At that time Kong Daofu, Ju Yong, Liu Sui, and Cao Xiugu in turn served as remonstrators and censors; Guo Quan and Duan Shaolian succeeded them—all spoke with open countenance and stern color, on encountering affairs always spoke, were expelled and driven away, and did not alter their steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kong Daofu, Ju Yong, Liu Sui, and Cao Xiugu served in turn as remonstrators and censors, followed by Guo Quan and Duan Shaolian. All spoke with forthright bearing, remonstrating on every issue; though expelled and driven out, none altered his principles.

sentences.zh: 及帝既親政，道輔、勸、少連復任言責，郭后之廢，引議慷慨，犯人主，責大臣，其氣益壯，遺風餘烈，天下至今稱之。

translations.literal: When the emperor had personally taken government, Daofu, Quan, and Shaolian again bore the duty of speech; on Empress Guo's deposition they argued with impassioned generosity, offending the ruler and reproaching great ministers—their spirit grew all the stronger; their lingering wind and remaining fierceness the realm praises to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor assumed personal rule, Daofu, Quan, and Shaolian again bore the duty of remonstrance. On the deposition of Empress Guo they argued with passionate courage, offending the throne and reproaching the chief ministers. Their spirit only grew stronger, and their legacy is praised throughout the realm to this day.

sentences.zh: 《詩》所謂「邦之司直」，其庶幾歟！

translations.literal: What the Odes calls "the state's rectifier"—they perhaps approached this!
translations.idiomatic: They perhaps approached what the Odes calls "the rectifiers of the state"!
